Jordan: FYI — ACME reports sudden drop in embeddings vectors/sec yesterday evening. Tokens/sec looks normal for text-gen requests but vector throughput halved. Can someone triage?
Aisha: On it. Do we have a customer repro payload + timeframe?
Jordan: Pasted payload and curl they used, timeframe ~2026-02-11 03:10-03:25 UTC.
Jordan: curl snippet:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d '{"model":"rw-embed-1024","input":["doc1","doc2",...],"batch_size":64}'
```
Aisha: Thanks. Quick check: customer says tokens/sec unchanged because they also call text-gen endpoints — only embed pipeline slow.
Kai: Pulling router logs + queue lengths for that window now. Initial guess: batching window got narrower after a recent autoscaler tweak so we might be hitting smaller batches -> lower vectors/sec.
Marta: Also check for dimension mismatch auto-fallbacks. If upstream switched model variant (1024->768), we might be falling back to per-request conversion and double-copying.
Riley: GPU metrics show a spike in GPU memcpy and low util on some hosts at 03:12 UTC — suggests kernel mismatch or excessive small kernels. Attaching log excerpt:
```
[03:12:08] host-gpu-12: kv_cache_shard=0 queue_depth=18 batch_size_avg=8 kernel_launchs=423 memcpy_ms=1240 util=32%
[03:12:09] host-gpu-12: InvalidEmbeddingDim: expected 1024 got 768 for model rw-embed-1024_variant_b
```
Aisha: That InvalidEmbeddingDim entry looks important. If model variant swapped, runtime may be doing on-the-fly upcast -> extra work.
Jordan: Customer insists they pinned model; but we should verify routing fallback logs.
Kai: Routing history for ACME shows fallback at 03:11:54 from rw-embed-1024 -> rw-embed-1024-quantized-b because of capacity pressure. Quantized variant has a different internal dim packing.
Marta: Quantized variant uses packed 768 lanes with different kernel path. If request batch_size=64 but per-worker continuous batching window decreased, we end up with many small kernel launches with padding. That will drop vectors/sec while tokens/sec (from other services) unaffected.
Aisha: Repro plan: 1) replay customer payload against rw-embed-1024 and rw-embed-1024-quantized-b locally 2) capture batch sizes, kernel launch counts 3) measure vectors/sec and GPU memcpy.
Riley: I started a quick local replay. Observed: when routing to quantized variant, vectors/sec ~45% lower and memcpy jumps. Patchy batch sizes (6-12) vs expected 48-64.
Jordan: Can you paste the replay command?
Riley:```bash
python tools/replay_embeddings.py --input acme_sample.json --model rw-embed-1024-quantized-b --concurrency 4 --batch-window-ms 20
```
Kai: Temporary mitigation for ACME: force routing to full-precision variant in their tenant config for the next 12h. Will that be acceptable?
Jordan: ACME ok with temporary route change if it restores SLA. They want root cause next.
Marta: Root cause hypothesis: autoscaler/capacity pressure triggered routing to a quantized variant with incompatible batching characteristics. Combined with a recent change to continuous batching window (reduced from 40ms to 20ms) -> smaller average batches -> kernel inefficiency + memcpy overhead -> vectors/sec drop. Also some requests hit a dimension-compatibility code path causing extra copies (InvalidEmbeddingDim warnings).
Aisha: Action items: 
- Kai: undo routing fallback for ACME tenant (apply override) - in progress
- Riley: reproduce + attach perf logs (kernel launches, memcpy, batch hist) - assigned
- Marta: open runtime ticket for dimension-fallback path and quantify cost penalty - assigned
- Jordan: notify customer with ETA and mitigation steps - assigned

Riley: Uploaded replay logs to /shared/support/1788881234/replay_logs.tar.gz. Key numbers: avg_batch=9 (quantized), avg_batch=56 (fp), vectors/sec_quant=1200, vectors/sec_fp=2650, gpu_util_quant=34%, gpu_util_fp=78%.
Kai: Override deployed — ACME traffic pinned to fp variant at 03:33 UTC. Monitoring shows vectors/sec recovered to baseline within two minutes.
Jordan: Customer notified and content with temporary fix. They're asking for a permanent prevention; they want a postmortem.
Marta: Will create postmortem draft and include: autoscaler->routing policy interaction, batching window change, quantized kernel inefficiencies, dimension-fallback penalty. Also add an e2e test that replays tenancy traffic across model variants and flags >20% drop in vectors/sec.
Aisha: Any low-risk short-term config change we can ship to avoid this for other tenants? Maybe prefer fp variant if batch_size>32 or concurrent requests high.
Kai: Agree. Will add routing heuristic: prefer variants with similar batching profiles when capacity pressure triggers fallback.
Jordan: Closing loop: ACME happy for now; next steps tracked in infra-ticket INF-4492. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
